title: Taruna Dal Pressure Leaves Lahore Exposed

blocks.text: This page closes the Taruna Dal episode by explaining how Sikh expansion after the Lahore-side raids kept widening the zone of Mughal weakness. So much land and revenue passed beyond effective control that the Lahore administration could no longer collect revenue with confidence outside the city itself.

The political consequence is immediate. What had looked like scattered Sikh mobility now appears as a structural threat to Lahore's ability to govern, punish, and tax the countryside that sustained it.

The page therefore serves as a bridge into the next confrontation. Ahmad Shah's side responds by sending stronger commanders into Punjab, preparing the entry of Sar Buland Khan and a more formal contest with the Khalsa.
